title: In the Heights ending discussion: @Joe Weinberg    📸 Valerie Terranov...
transcript: Don't mind me, just crying through my 2nd-favorite musical of all time. Last night I was invited to the gala opening of in the Heights, which actually marks the first time City Centre has revived a musical whose original production I personally saw. And what a joy it was to see it again. I mean, it's hard to mess up in the Heights, but still. This production from exodus director David Mendizábal captures the love and exuberance in this musical. With a story by Quiara Alegria Hudes that's as heartwarming as it is heartbreaking and a true no skip masterpiece score from Lin Manuel Miranda. This production actually features a bunch of super talented young actors I had never heard of. The highlights for me being Aaron James McKenzie as Benny and Ishmael Gonzalez with a new and delightful take on Sonny. But I think the main performance stand out for me was Tony winnerNatalie Belcon as Claudia. I actually made a video recently about how  the character of Claudia deviates from the “wise old grandma” trope in a couple key ways. Interestingly, Belcon is now older than Olga Merediz was when she played the role originally. But Belcon's performance, along with the costume and wig design, really emphasized that Claudia is still not that old in the grand scheme of things and living a full and active life. Aside from a couple cool moments of staging and design, especially in Blackout, there wasn't a whole lot else that stood out to me about the direction of this production. And you know, I've been saying for a while now that it's gotten more difficult to engage critically with these City Center “concert” productions because they *almost* feel like full productions. So they invite those standards in comparisons, but just aren't quite as locked in or fully realized as a traditional production would be, with a full rehearsal process. But that's not specific to in the Heights. And in any case, I did still enjoy it immensely. My love for this show just continues to deepen as I get older. Like, for example, on this viewing, I found myself more moved than ever before by Kevin's character arc. And for a little lore drop fun fact, my emotional nostalgia for this musical has a little bit of irony: The themes of home make me feel a little homesick for San Francisco, where I grew up. And yet I left San Francisco to live in Washington Heights. Kind of the reverse of what Nina does. But after eight years here, I also have a deep love for Washington Heights, so the layers just keep piling on for me.
